docs.t: Judge Donovan W. Frank (D. Minn.) — Scheduling order spacing (trap)
docs.x: Judge Donovan W. Frank, D. Minn.. Scheduling order spacing (trap): Dispositive motions must be filed before the scheduling-order deadline, which is typically a “served and filed” (not heard) date. The trial-ready date should be 150 days after that deadline, to allow a ruling, trial preparation, and settlement efforts without losing the trial date.

docs.t: Judge Donovan W. Frank (D. Minn.) — Special motions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Donovan W. Frank, D. Minn.. Special motions (trap): Motions to transfer, remand, and compel arbitration are briefed as dispositive motions. TRO papers must be filed before a hearing is set, and two courtesy copies must go to chambers immediately after e-filing. Judge Frank hears Daubert motions personally, generally at the pretrial conference; if the parties agree a Daubert ruling would be dispositive of an issue, contact the courtroom deputy to set an earlier hearing. Discovery motions go to the magistrate judge. Patent cases use Local Rule Form 4 for the Rule 26(f) report.

docs.t: Judge Donovan W. Frank (D. Minn.) — Written submissions and courtesy copies (trap)
docs.x: Judge Donovan W. Frank, D. Minn.. Written submissions and courtesy copies (trap): Word count and format rules are strictly enforced. Request extra space by letter to the court, filed on ECF well in advance, not after exceeding the limit; filing a motion per count to gain space is discouraged. E-filed exhibits need a separate exhibit index. Complete transcripts of key depositions are encouraged over excerpts, and hyperlinked, searchable briefs and exhibits are preferred. Send two courtesy copies of motion papers, collated as two sets, tabbed, three-hole punched, and bound, stapled, or clamped (binders welcome for voluminous filings), preferably with the NEF header; this applies to conventional filings too. Sealed documents: two three-hole-punched courtesy copies, no separate envelopes.

docs.t: Judge Donovan W. Frank (D. Minn.) — Oral argument conduct
docs.x: Judge Donovan W. Frank, D. Minn.. Oral argument conduct: The judge reads everything in advance; don’t repeat facts, focus on key issues, and expect questions. Stand at the podium and address the court, not the law clerk. Contact the courtroom deputy in advance to use courtroom technology; training is available. New case law at argument must first go to opposing counsel, with two extra copies of cases or handouts for the court.

docs.t: Judge Donovan W. Frank (D. Minn.) — Newer lawyers
docs.x: Judge Donovan W. Frank, D. Minn.. Newer lawyers: Lawyers with less than five years’ experience are strongly encouraged to argue and examine witnesses. The court may allow split argument and relax the one-lawyer-per-witness rule at trial; contact the courtroom deputy at least one week before the hearing or trial.

docs.t: Judge Donovan W. Frank (D. Minn.) — Trial (trap)
docs.x: Judge Donovan W. Frank, D. Minn.. Trial (trap): A trial notice issues about three months before the trial-ready date. In jury trials, statements of the case, exhibit and witness lists, deposition designations, motions in limine, proposed voir dire, and proposed jury instructions are due 10 days before the pretrial conference; responses to motions in limine 3 days before trial. A trial management order follows. Jointly submit jury instructions with citations: agreed instructions in black ink, disputed ones in each party’s color (red for plaintiff, blue for defendant). Most should be agreed. Preliminary instructions previewing the legal issues are encouraged, as is a joint statement of the case to read during voir dire. Mark exhibits to match the exhibit list, preferably grouped by witness, and deliver one set of hard copies to chambers in tabbed binders before trial. The court asks the pa

docs.t: Judge Donovan W. Frank (D. Minn.) — Settlement conferences
docs.x: Judge Donovan W. Frank, D. Minn.. Settlement conferences: All settlement conferences go to the magistrate judge; request one any time. More than one is allowed.

docs.t: Judge Eric C. Tostrud (D. Minn.) — Getting a hearing date (trap)
docs.x: Judge Eric C. Tostrud, D. Minn.. Getting a hearing date (trap): Judge Tostrud follows Local Rule 7.1 for civil motions. Get a hearing date shortly before filing by emailing the courtroom deputy at Tostrud_Chambers@mnd.uscourts.gov with the file number, type of motion, filing date, and all pending or anticipated motions so they can be heard together. After the deputy gives a date, confirm that it works for all other parties before issuing a notice of hearing.

docs.t: Judge Eric C. Tostrud (D. Minn.) — In-person hearings
docs.x: Judge Eric C. Tostrud, D. Minn.. In-person hearings: All civil hearings are in person unless an exceptional circumstance keeps a party from the courthouse; tell the court if there is one.

docs.t: Judge Eric C. Tostrud (D. Minn.) — Courtesy copies (trap)
docs.x: Judge Eric C. Tostrud, D. Minn.. Courtesy copies (trap): Two courtesy copies of memoranda and one of supporting documents, mailed or delivered to the clerk’s office in St. Paul the next business day after filing, addressed to Chief Judge Tostrud. Copies must be three-hole punched, unstapled, double-sided if feasible, and, if voluminous, tabbed and in binders. Include the docket number, most easily by printing the filed version with the CM/ECF header.

docs.t: Judge Eric C. Tostrud (D. Minn.) — Oral argument
docs.x: Judge Eric C. Tostrud, D. Minn.. Oral argument: Each side typically gets 20 minutes. Multiple plaintiffs or multiple defendants split their side’s time. More time may be granted in the court’s discretion on a party’s prior request.

docs.t: Judge Jeffrey Bryan (D. Minn.) — General (trap)
docs.x: Judge Jeffrey Bryan, D. Minn.. General (trap): Contact chambers only through the courtroom deputy at bryan_chambers@mnd.uscourts.gov, not the law clerks, on case-specific matters. Noncompliant requests will be denied, pleadings struck, and documents disregarded. Some of these practices depart from the Local Rules. Judge Bryan recuses from cases in which spouse Liz Kramer, an attorney, represents a party or that otherwise present an ethical conflict from that relationship.

docs.t: Judge Jeffrey Bryan (D. Minn.) — Dispositive motion scheduling (trap)
docs.x: Judge Jeffrey Bryan, D. Minn.. Dispositive motion scheduling (trap): Email the deputy, copying opposing counsel, at least 10 days before the filing deadline. State the motion’s nature, other pending motions here and in related cases, whether any party plans a cross-motion for summary judgment, whether you want a decision without a hearing, and anything else the deputy needs. The deputy gives a filing date for the motion and brief (typically 49 days before the hearing) and hearing-date options; the parties confer and jointly report their preference. File the notice of hearing and meet-and-confer statement separately, any time after getting the dates; that filing meets the motion deadline under the FRCP or scheduling order. File the rest of the L.R. 7.1(c)(1) papers on the assigned filing date. No editable proposed orders unless the deputy asks.

docs.t: Judge Jeffrey Bryan (D. Minn.) — Briefing deadlines and word limits (trap)
docs.x: Judge Jeffrey Bryan, D. Minn.. Briefing deadlines and word limits (trap): Local Rule 7.1 response and reply deadlines are enforced; motions to change them are strongly discouraged and denied absent exceptional circumstances. Requests to enlarge page or word limits are disfavored and must be made by motion on ECF at least 7 days before the filing deadline.

docs.t: Judge Jeffrey Bryan (D. Minn.) — Early summary judgment and Daubert
docs.x: Judge Jeffrey Bryan, D. Minn.. Early summary judgment and Daubert: Summary judgment before the close of discovery requires permission, requested by email to the deputy. A Daubert motion that could eliminate a claim or defense is filed with the dispositive motion, and all such Daubert motions plus the dispositive motion count as a single motion for the L.R. 7.1(f) word limit. Other Daubert motions are motions in limine under the trial order.

docs.t: Judge Jeffrey Bryan (D. Minn.) — Injunctive relief (trap)
docs.x: Judge Jeffrey Bryan, D. Minn.. Injunctive relief (trap): File and serve the motion first, then email the deputy with complete contact information for all other parties. The court will strike a motion that fails to (1) state in its title and text whether it is under Rule 65(a) or 65(b), (2) say whether the movant seeks to present witness testimony, (3) list all relief requested in detail, and (4) cite supporting record facts (verified complaint or affidavit). The court decides the rule that applies, the schedule, and whether to allow live testimony, and may order an expedited conference with the magistrate judge.

docs.t: Judge Jeffrey Bryan (D. Minn.) — Filings and consent decrees
docs.x: Judge Jeffrey Bryan, D. Minn.. Filings and consent decrees: No courtesy copies unless requested, which may happen with extensive briefing or voluminous exhibits. File complete deposition and other transcripts, and file each exhibit as a separate ECF attachment. Consent judgments and decrees are not needed in most private civil disputes; a proposed one must include authority and argument showing it is fair, reasonable, and consistent with governing law.

docs.t: Judge Jeffrey Bryan (D. Minn.) — Hearings (trap)
docs.x: Judge Jeffrey Bryan, D. Minn.. Hearings (trap): Arrive at least 15 minutes early. Each side typically gets 15 minutes; email the deputy at least 7 days ahead for more time. Slides or other visual aids for a hearing or trial: send one electronic copy to opposing counsel and a PDF to the deputy at least 7 days before the hearing. Case law not in the briefs must go to opposing counsel before the court. Newer attorneys are encouraged to present; the judge allows bifurcated arguments and assistance from more experienced counsel. You may email the deputy for time to practice with courtroom technology.

docs.t: Judge Jeffrey Bryan (D. Minn.) — Criminal pretrial and pleas (trap)
docs.x: Judge Jeffrey Bryan, D. Minn.. Criminal pretrial and pleas (trap): The government is responsible for Speedy Trial Act compliance and should file discovery motions as soon as possible after initial appearance. After all dispositive pretrial motions are resolved, the parties meet and confer, and within 7 days the government files either a joint motion to exclude time with a statement of reasons or a status letter confirming no exclusion is needed, readiness for trial, and estimated length. Absent agreement, the party seeking exclusion moves within 7 days. For a plea agreement, email the deputy the draft agreement and request a change-of-plea date, noting any Guidelines disagreements in the agreement. If the plea cannot be put in writing, request a status conference first; beforehand the government files a Statement of the Case covering the factual basis for each element, Guidelines facts,

docs.t: Judge Jeffrey Bryan (D. Minn.) — Sentencing (trap)
docs.x: Judge Jeffrey Bryan, D. Minn.. Sentencing (trap): Judge Bryan departs from parts of L.R. 83.10. Contact the deputy promptly after the final presentence report to schedule sentencing. Positions Regarding Sentencing are due at least 14 days before the hearing, and a motion for a contested evidentiary hearing is due within 14 days after the final PSR is filed. Tell the deputy in advance about any witness testimony or victims who will speak. Defense counsel must review proposed supervised-release conditions with the defendant beforehand; if the defendant waives having each read, the court will not read them into the record.

docs.t: Judge Jeffrey Bryan (D. Minn.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge Jeffrey Bryan, D. Minn.. Trial: A trial notice with deadlines issues about four weeks before a criminal trial and about five months before a civil trial. Motions in limine are typically decided after the pretrial conference, but parties may ask for earlier rulings, especially where they would change the time and expense of trial preparation. Parties must meet and confer to jointly submit trial documents and stipulate to as many exhibits as possible. Contacting jurors after trial requires the judge’s written permission.

docs.t: Judge Jerry W. Blackwell (D. Minn.) — Contact with chambers (trap)
docs.x: Judge Jerry W. Blackwell, D. Minn.. Contact with chambers (trap): Direct questions to the courtroom deputy (651-848-1160), not the law clerks. Except in an emergency, calls and emails are limited to scheduling and the judge’s preferences and procedures; check the ECF docket first. No ex parte communication on substantive matters. Raise them by formal motion or an ECF letter of no more than two pages, and file a letter only after requesting permission from chambers in writing and receiving it.

docs.t: Judge Jerry W. Blackwell (D. Minn.) — Extensions and adjournments (trap)
docs.x: Judge Jerry W. Blackwell, D. Minn.. Extensions and adjournments (trap): Do not call to ask for an adjournment or extension except in an emergency. Requests must be in writing, filed on ECF at least two business days before the deadline or appearance. State the original date, the reason, the time needed, the number and outcome of prior requests by either party, that you first conferred with all parties on alternative dates, whether the adversary consents (and its reasons if not), and any agreed alternative dates. Attach a proposed Amended Scheduling Order if other dates are affected.

docs.t: Judge Jerry W. Blackwell (D. Minn.) — Motion scheduling
docs.x: Judge Jerry W. Blackwell, D. Minn.. Motion scheduling: A party filing a Rule 12 motion instead of an answer should be ready to argue it 42 days after filing or soon after. Before filing a dispositive motion, contact the deputy, preferably by email to Blackwell_Chambers@mnd.uscourts.gov. Tell the deputy about all pending motions, and related motions in related cases, so they are heard together. Each party filing or opposing a dispositive civil motion must submit a proposed order under Standing Order No. 3, which adds to Local Rule 7.1.

docs.t: Judge Jerry W. Blackwell (D. Minn.) — TROs and summary judgment
docs.x: Judge Jerry W. Blackwell, D. Minn.. TROs and summary judgment: File the TRO papers first, with a Notice of Hearing showing a “To Be Determined” date, then contact chambers to request a telephone status conference. If a hearing is set, promptly file and serve a notice of hearing. TRO, preliminary injunction, and Daubert motions are generally heard without witness testimony absent advance permission. No summary judgment motion before the discovery deadline without prior permission; a denial is not a view on the merits.

docs.t: Judge Jerry W. Blackwell (D. Minn.) — Briefs and pleadings (trap)
docs.x: Judge Jerry W. Blackwell, D. Minn.. Briefs and pleadings (trap): Judge Blackwell reviews complaints for Rule 8 compliance. No brief over the Local Rule word limit without prior permission, sought well before the deadline by an ECF letter concisely stating the basis. Do not use explanatory letters or multiple simultaneous dispositive motions to gain briefing space (L.R. 7.1(c)(4)). When a deadline falls on a weekend, file the following Monday.

docs.t: Judge Jerry W. Blackwell (D. Minn.) — Courtesy copies and transcripts (trap)
docs.x: Judge Jerry W. Blackwell, D. Minn.. Courtesy copies and transcripts (trap): If briefs, declarations, and exhibits total 100 or more pages, submit one printed courtesy copy: tabbed, single-sided, three-hole punched, and unstapled. A brief relying on 100 or more pages of exhibits, affidavits, or declarations also requires a hyperlinked electronic courtesy copy under Standing Order No. 2. Deposition excerpts should include at least three pages before and after each excerpt; if excerpts and bookends exceed half the transcript, submit it all. Printed transcripts in courtesy copies go four pages per sheet.

docs.t: Judge Jerry W. Blackwell (D. Minn.) — Oral argument
docs.x: Judge Jerry W. Blackwell, D. Minn.. Oral argument: Arrive at least 15 minutes early; hearings start on time. Stand at the podium and use titles and last names. Bring printed copies of any PowerPoint for opposing counsel and two for the judge and staff, and do not use slides as a script. New case law goes to opposing counsel first; bring two extra copies of cases or handouts. The judge reads all submissions in advance.

docs.t: Judge Jerry W. Blackwell (D. Minn.) — Newer attorneys
docs.x: Judge Jerry W. Blackwell, D. Minn.. Newer attorneys: Lead counsel are strongly encouraged to let attorneys with six or fewer years of experience, and diverse attorneys, examine witnesses and argue. More experienced counsel may be allowed to assist a junior lawyer during argument. The judge may decide a matter on the papers without a hearing unless an attorney with six or fewer years of experience will argue it. All attorneys must be prepared and have appropriate authority to speak for the client.

docs.t: Judge Jerry W. Blackwell (D. Minn.) — Miscellaneous
docs.x: Judge Jerry W. Blackwell, D. Minn.. Miscellaneous: Use the name “Jerry W. Blackwell” in proposed orders. Parties must also follow the judge’s Standing Orders at www.mnd.uscourts.gov/JWB.

docs.t: Judge Joan N. Ericksen (D. Minn.) — Dispositive motion scheduling (trap)
docs.x: Judge Joan N. Ericksen, D. Minn.. Dispositive motion scheduling (trap): Do not call for a hearing date until ready to file the motion. Once the date is set, the response is due 21 days after the motion is filed and the reply 14 days after that. The movant must include these dates in the notice of motion.

docs.t: Judge Joan N. Ericksen (D. Minn.) — Written submissions and courtesy copies
docs.x: Judge Joan N. Ericksen, D. Minn.. Written submissions and courtesy copies: File during regular business hours on the due date if possible. Counsel are personally responsible for redaction compliance in exhibits and attachments, and for making courtesy-copy exhibits organized and readily locatable; loose, untabbed, unpaginated, or top-pronged and upside-down documents do not qualify. Three-ring binders are welcome but not required.

docs.t: Judge Joan N. Ericksen (D. Minn.) — Oral argument
docs.x: Judge Joan N. Ericksen, D. Minn.. Oral argument: Argument is generally scheduled for 30 minutes per side.

docs.t: Judge Joan N. Ericksen (D. Minn.) — Contact with chambers
docs.x: Judge Joan N. Ericksen, D. Minn.. Contact with chambers: Chambers staff answer questions about logistics, procedure, and technology through JoanEricksen_Chambers@mnd.uscourts.gov. Do not email the judge or the law clerks directly.

docs.t: Judge John R. Tunheim (D. Minn.) — Motion scheduling (trap)
docs.x: Judge John R. Tunheim, D. Minn.. Motion scheduling (trap): Hearings are scheduled only after the motion is filed and fully briefed. Once briefing is complete, email or call the courtroom deputy to request a date; the deputy will generally email a suggested date when the court is ready. Attorneys are responsible for filing in compliance with the Local Rules. Judge Tunheim hears Daubert motions and usually holds Markman hearings personally; schedule Markman before summary judgment. Dispositive motions are occasionally referred to the magistrate judge, case by case.

docs.t: Judge John R. Tunheim (D. Minn.) — Written submissions and courtesy copies
docs.x: Judge John R. Tunheim, D. Minn.. Written submissions and courtesy copies: Follow the Local Rules’ page or word limits and filing procedures. No courtesy copies of anything filed on CM/ECF are required. Page or word extensions may be requested by motion or letter, in advance.

docs.t: Judge John R. Tunheim (D. Minn.) — Oral argument
docs.x: Judge John R. Tunheim, D. Minn.. Oral argument: Motion hearings run 20 minutes per side unless more time is permitted. Stand at the podium and be formal unless told otherwise. Don’t repeat the facts in the briefs; focus on the key disputed issues and be ready for questions. Courtroom technology is encouraged where appropriate. Additional case law offered at or after argument must first go to opposing counsel; if submitted the day of argument, bring two copies for the court.

docs.t: Judge John R. Tunheim (D. Minn.) — Newer and diverse lawyers (standing order)
docs.x: Judge John R. Tunheim, D. Minn.. Newer and diverse lawyers (standing order): The Standing Order on Diversity in the Courtroom (issued as Chief Judge) permits oral argument on most dispositive civil motions and most criminal motions and encourages letting less experienced lawyers, particularly women and members of underrepresented communities who are integral to the team, argue motions. Split arguments are allowed on request. At trial, newer lawyers are encouraged to give openings and closings, question witnesses, and argue motions or jury instructions. The order is not meant to encourage unnecessary motions.

docs.t: Judge John R. Tunheim (D. Minn.) — Trial (trap)
docs.x: Judge John R. Tunheim, D. Minn.. Trial (trap): A Notice of Trial and a Memorandum with instructions on when trial papers are due issue six weeks before trial. Motions in limine are generally argued before jury selection on day one, though the court may set an earlier hearing and parties may request one; not every motion in limine will be argued. The judge conducts voir dire. Attorneys must use the courtroom technology for all trial proceedings and be trained on it; other technology must be pre-approved. Contact the courtroom deputy to schedule training and practice time. For proceedings in Duluth or Fergus Falls, contact the courtroom deputy about courtroom technology.

docs.t: Judge John R. Tunheim (D. Minn.) — Transcripts
docs.x: Judge John R. Tunheim, D. Minn.. Transcripts: Contact the court reporter, Kristine Mousseau, before any trial or hearing if requesting realtime or daily copy, with as much lead time as possible.

docs.t: Judge John R. Tunheim (D. Minn.) — Juror contact
docs.x: Judge John R. Tunheim, D. Minn.. Juror contact: Post-trial juror contact requires the judge’s written permission in all cases. If granted, contact is by letter only, not telephone, though jurors may call the attorneys in response.

docs.t: Judge John R. Tunheim (D. Minn.) — Settlement and chambers contact
docs.x: Judge John R. Tunheim, D. Minn.. Settlement and chambers contact: All settlement conferences go to the magistrate judge; request one any time through the magistrate judge. The judge may ask the magistrate judge to hold more. Contact the courtroom deputy, not the law clerks.

docs.t: Judge Katherine M. Menendez (D. Minn.) — Scheduling hearings (trap)
docs.x: Judge Katherine M. Menendez, D. Minn.. Scheduling hearings (trap): Schedule all motions through the courtroom deputy at 612-664-5140, saying when you expect to be ready to file. Tell the deputy about all pending or anticipated motions and any related motions in related cases, and alert the other side before you call. Hearings are usually set no sooner than two weeks after briefing closes, unless expedited. Even if the hearing is months out, you must file by the scheduling-order deadline and file all L.R. 7.1(b) or 7.1(c) documents at the same time. If the parties agree a motion can be decided on the papers, say so in the Notice of Hearing; the judge may still hold a hearing. To reschedule, have all counsel on the line at once.

docs.t: Judge Katherine M. Menendez (D. Minn.) — Contact with chambers
docs.x: Judge Katherine M. Menendez, D. Minn.. Contact with chambers: Chambers will not answer legal questions, including procedural questions governed by the FRCP, the Local Rules, or the scheduling order, and will not talk to the media. For a question about or clarification of an order, do not call; file a letter on CM/ECF. When calling about a case, identify yourself and your party and have the case name and number ready. CM/ECF filing questions go to the Clerk’s help desk at 612-664-5155.

docs.t: Judge Katherine M. Menendez (D. Minn.) — Courtesy copies and sealed filings (trap)
docs.x: Judge Katherine M. Menendez, D. Minn.. Courtesy copies and sealed filings (trap): No courtesy copies of motion papers, except for sealed filings the court cannot view on CM/ECF. Those must be hand-delivered to the Clerk’s Office, on paper or a data storage device, the same day they are filed. Sealed filings must follow Local Rule 5.6.

docs.t: Judge Katherine M. Menendez (D. Minn.) — Remote proceedings and status conferences
docs.x: Judge Katherine M. Menendez, D. Minn.. Remote proceedings and status conferences: Zoom requests go by email to menendez_chambers@mnd.uscourts.gov, copying opposing counsel. Agreement of both sides is ideal but not required, and the judge may order remote proceedings. The judge may set telephonic status conferences; for a conflict, call the deputy or email chambers to reschedule.

docs.t: Judge Katherine M. Menendez (D. Minn.) — Summary judgment and Daubert (trap)
docs.x: Judge Katherine M. Menendez, D. Minn.. Summary judgment and Daubert (trap): No summary judgment motion before the discovery deadline without leave, and no more than one summary judgment motion per party in a case without permission. Judge Menendez generally hears Daubert motions. One that would eliminate a claim or defense is filed with the dispositive motion and argued in the same memoranda, counting as one motion for the L.R. 7.1(f) word limit; one that only limits trial testimony is a motion in limine under the trial notice.

docs.t: Judge Katherine M. Menendez (D. Minn.) — TROs and expedited proceedings
docs.x: Judge Katherine M. Menendez, D. Minn.. TROs and expedited proceedings: Email a full set of papers to chambers the same day the motion is filed on ECF, serve the other side, and email contact information for both sides. The court then sets the hearing date and briefing schedule.

docs.t: Judge Katherine M. Menendez (D. Minn.) — Oral argument (trap)
docs.x: Judge Katherine M. Menendez, D. Minn.. Oral argument (trap): The judge reads the papers in advance and is likely to spend the hearing asking questions rather than hearing a prepared presentation. Email visual aids (e.g., PowerPoint) to the court and opposing counsel no later than the day before; no paper copies needed, and you may not get to present them. New case law or exhibits must go to opposing counsel first, with two copies for the court, but the judge prefers they be emailed to the court and counsel at least a day ahead. Newer lawyers who drafted or contributed significantly to the papers are strongly encouraged to argue; email ahead for accommodations such as divided time or consulting experienced counsel.

docs.t: Judge Katherine M. Menendez (D. Minn.) — Courtroom logistics
docs.x: Judge Katherine M. Menendez, D. Minn.. Courtroom logistics: Arrive early and double-check the location: the judge sits in Minneapolis but sometimes uses other courtrooms or courthouses. Address the court from the center podium into the microphone. Water is generally not provided except to witnesses and criminal defendants; lidded beverages are allowed. Learn the courtroom technology in advance and bring your own adapters; basic training can be arranged through the deputy. Have a back-up plan, since chambers is not responsible for the technology.

docs.t: Judge Laura Provinzino (D. Minn.) — Motion hearings (trap)
docs.x: Judge Laura Provinzino, D. Minn.. Motion hearings (trap): Do not call for a hearing date or file a Notice of Hearing with the motion. The court schedules hearings after filing, typically after the response; the courtroom deputy emails a suggested date, and the court issues the Notice of Hearing. If the parties agree a motion can be decided on the papers, they should file a Notice of Hearing saying so; the judge may still order a hearing. Contact the deputy at provinzino_chambers@mnd.uscourts.gov; the deputy answers questions about the judge’s practices but gives no legal advice.

docs.t: Judge Laura Provinzino (D. Minn.) — Meet and confer (trap)
docs.x: Judge Laura Provinzino, D. Minn.. Meet and confer (trap): The L.R. 7.1(a) meet-and-confer statement must state how the parties met (in person, video, telephone, or email), the date, and how long they discussed the motion.

docs.t: Judge Laura Provinzino (D. Minn.) — Motion types and Daubert
docs.x: Judge Laura Provinzino, D. Minn.. Motion types and Daubert: Motions to remand, transfer venue, and compel arbitration are briefed as dispositive motions, and Daubert and Markman motions are treated as dispositive. A Daubert motion that would eliminate a claim or defense is filed with the dispositive motion and argued in the same memoranda, counting as one motion for the L.R. 7.1(f) word limit. One that only limits trial testimony is a motion in limine.

docs.t: Judge Laura Provinzino (D. Minn.) — TROs and evidentiary hearings
docs.x: Judge Laura Provinzino, D. Minn.. TROs and evidentiary hearings: File the motion and papers, serve the other side, and email the deputy with contact information for all parties; the court then sets any hearing and briefing schedule. TROs, preliminary injunctions, and Daubert motions are typically heard without testimony. To present witnesses, notify the court and the other side and provide witness and exhibit lists as soon as possible, no later than three court days before the hearing.

docs.t: Judge Laura Provinzino (D. Minn.) — Early summary judgment (trap)
docs.x: Judge Laura Provinzino, D. Minn.. Early summary judgment (trap): Summary judgment before the close of discovery requires permission sought by a letter of no more than three pages stating the relief, whether fully or partially dispositive, whether the request is opposed, and why early consideration is warranted (specifying fact or expert discovery). The opponent may respond with a letter of no more than three pages within seven days. Denial is not a view on the merits.

docs.t: Judge Laura Provinzino (D. Minn.) — Briefs and exhibits (trap)
docs.x: Judge Laura Provinzino, D. Minn.. Briefs and exhibits (trap): Motions to enlarge word limits are disfavored and must be filed at least three court days before the brief is due (L.R. 7.1(f)(1)(D)); do not file the longer brief until the request is granted. No courtesy copies unless requested. Digital media goes to the Clerk’s Office on a storage device. File each exhibit as a separate ECF attachment with a brief description, in searchable form where possible. Use full-page deposition transcripts, not compact (four-to-a-page) versions. Excerpts must include the cover page, the signature or verification page, and at least two pages before and after each excerpt.

docs.t: Judge Laura Provinzino (D. Minn.) — Supplemental authority
docs.x: Judge Laura Provinzino, D. Minn.. Supplemental authority: No advance permission needed. File a letter brief of no more than three pages explaining the authority’s relevance, with a copy of the authority; the opponent may respond with a letter of no more than three pages within seven days.

docs.t: Judge Laura Provinzino (D. Minn.) — Hearings and remote appearances
docs.x: Judge Laura Provinzino, D. Minn.. Hearings and remote appearances: Hearings are in person unless otherwise indicated, in Courtroom 3A at the St. Paul courthouse (check the location, which may vary). Remote hearings may be requested from the deputy but require good cause. Arrive at least 15 minutes early; hearings start on time. Stand at the lectern and observe formal decorum. For real-time or daily copy transcripts, email court reporter Lynne Krenz (lynne_krenz@mnd.uscourts.gov) before the trial or hearing, with as much lead time as possible.

docs.t: Judge Laura Provinzino (D. Minn.) — Oral argument (trap)
docs.x: Judge Laura Provinzino, D. Minn.. Oral argument (trap): Argument is a back-and-forth discussion, not a summary of the briefs; be ready for detailed questions about the record. There is no set time limit, but about 15 minutes per side is the benchmark. PowerPoint may not summarize or restate arguments or add new arguments or evidence; it may only highlight parts of the record. Email visual aids (other than filed exhibits) and any new legal authority to the court and opposing counsel at least one court day before the hearing. The judge prefers that the attorney who drafted or contributed significantly to the papers argue, and freely accommodates newer attorneys (divided time, bifurcated argument, consultation, or a few extra minutes for experienced counsel) on email request to the deputy.

docs.t: Judge Laura Provinzino (D. Minn.) — Trial and settlement
docs.x: Judge Laura Provinzino, D. Minn.. Trial and settlement: Be ready for trial by the magistrate judge’s trial readiness date, which is not a date certain. After summary judgment rulings, the deputy schedules a status conference to discuss trial dates, and a Trial Notice with deadlines follows; samples are at mnd.uscourts.gov/LMP. All settlement conferences go to the assigned magistrate judge, and more than one may be held.

docs.t: Judge Michael J. Davis (D. Minn.) — Contact with chambers
docs.x: Judge Michael J. Davis, D. Minn.. Contact with chambers: Contact the courtroom deputy at 612-664-5070, not the law clerks.

docs.t: Judge Michael J. Davis (D. Minn.) — Motion scheduling (trap)
docs.x: Judge Michael J. Davis, D. Minn.. Motion scheduling (trap): Follows the Local Rules for scheduling; all moving papers must be ready to file before you get a hearing date. Civil motions are typically heard Thursdays, with multiple hearings set for the same time; the judge sets the order just before the hearing, so check in with the courtroom deputy. Parties with several motions that day should agree on their order in advance. Dispositive motions are argued at least 42 days after the motion papers are filed, and often later. Dispositive motions are occasionally referred to the magistrate judge, case by case. No summary judgment motion before the discovery deadline without special permission from the court. File motions or stipulations to extend deadlines well in advance, leaving the court time to review the fully briefed motion before the hearing.

docs.t: Judge Michael J. Davis (D. Minn.) — TROs and Daubert
docs.x: Judge Michael J. Davis, D. Minn.. TROs and Daubert: For expedited matters such as a TRO, submit two sets of courtesy copies the same day the motion is e-filed, serve the other side, and give chambers contact information for both sides; the court then sets the hearing date and briefing schedule. Judge Davis hears Daubert motions personally. Call the courtroom deputy to schedule one after expert reports are filed but well before the motion in limine deadline. TRO, preliminary injunction, and Daubert motions are heard without witness testimony absent advance permission.

docs.t: Judge Michael J. Davis (D. Minn.) — Written submissions and courtesy copies (trap)
docs.x: Judge Michael J. Davis, D. Minn.. Written submissions and courtesy copies (trap): Follow the Local Rules’ word and page limits. Do not file a separate motion for each count to gain briefing space. Extensions are disfavored and require an advance written request. Send two courtesy copies of motion papers, organized, tabbed as appropriate, three-hole punched, and bound, stapled, or clamped; filings over 1.5 inches must be tabbed in a binder. Do not wrap sealed copies separately; put them in the proper binders. Pay particular attention to the Local Rules and ECF rules on sealed and redacted filings.

docs.t: Judge Michael J. Davis (D. Minn.) — Oral argument
docs.x: Judge Michael J. Davis, D. Minn.. Oral argument: Generally no more than 15 minutes per side on dispositive motions. Arrive at least 15 minutes early to check in; stand at the podium and be formal. The judge reads the briefs in advance, so don’t repeat the facts. New case law offered at argument must first go to opposing counsel, with 2 copies for the court. Use the courtroom technology; the courtroom deputy can arrange training.

docs.t: Judge Michael J. Davis (D. Minn.) — Newer lawyers
docs.x: Judge Michael J. Davis, D. Minn.. Newer lawyers: Judge Davis encourages newer lawyers to argue motions and examine witnesses at trial, and will allow bifurcated argument to give them the chance. Contact chambers with questions.

docs.t: Judge Michael J. Davis (D. Minn.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge Michael J. Davis, D. Minn.. Trial: Meet and confer before trial and jointly submit the agreed jury instructions; stipulate to as many exhibits as possible. Attorney voir dire is by request; if granted, generally 10–15 minutes per side. Videotaped depositions must be edited down to the heart of the matter, or their use will be curtailed. Trial days generally run 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., with two 15-minute breaks and an hour for lunch; have enough witnesses to fill each day until 5:00 p.m. Stand and use the counsel-table microphones for objections; examine from the lectern; no permission needed to approach a witness. Provide a clean exhibit list for the jury before deliberations listing only admitted exhibits, reviewed by both sides and the court. Post-trial juror contact requires the judge’s written permission in all cases.

docs.t: Judge Michael J. Davis (D. Minn.) — Settlement conferences
docs.x: Judge Michael J. Davis, D. Minn.. Settlement conferences: All settlement conferences go to the magistrate judge (complicated cases may also go to a special master). Request one any time through the magistrate judge; the court often orders additional conferences before trial.

docs.t: Judge Nancy E. Brasel (D. Minn.) — Motion scheduling (trap)
docs.x: Judge Nancy E. Brasel, D. Minn.. Motion scheduling (trap): Judge Brasel follows the Local Rules for dispositive motion hearings, but all moving papers must be ready to file before you get a hearing date. The response is due 21 days after the motion is filed and the reply 14 days after the response. Unless expedited, argument on a dispositive motion is at least 42 days after the motion papers are filed. Motions are typically heard Mondays and Wednesdays. Tell the courtroom deputy (612-664-5050; not the law clerks) about all pending motions in the case, and any related motions in related cases, so they can be heard together.

docs.t: Judge Nancy E. Brasel (D. Minn.) — Motion types and early summary judgment (trap)
docs.x: Judge Nancy E. Brasel, D. Minn.. Motion types and early summary judgment (trap): Motions to transfer, remand, and compel arbitration are briefed as dispositive motions. All discovery motions go to the magistrate judge. No summary judgment motion before the discovery deadline without special permission. For a default judgment motion, plaintiff must serve the defendant and file a certificate of service on ECF before the hearing.

docs.t: Judge Nancy E. Brasel (D. Minn.) — Daubert motions
docs.x: Judge Nancy E. Brasel, D. Minn.. Daubert motions: Judge Brasel hears Daubert motions. One that would eliminate a claim or defense must be filed with the dispositive motion and argued in the same memoranda; the two count as a single motion for the L.R. 7.1(f) word limit. One that only limits trial testimony is brought as a motion in limine under the trial notice, which issues after the final ruling on dispositive motions and a final settlement conference.

docs.t: Judge Nancy E. Brasel (D. Minn.) — TROs and evidentiary hearings
docs.x: Judge Nancy E. Brasel, D. Minn.. TROs and evidentiary hearings: For a TRO or other expedited hearing, serve the motion and contact chambers with contact information for both sides; the court reviews the papers and sets the hearing and briefing schedule. TROs, preliminary injunctions, and Daubert motions are heard without witness testimony absent advance permission.

docs.t: Judge Nancy E. Brasel (D. Minn.) — Filings and briefs (trap)
docs.x: Judge Nancy E. Brasel, D. Minn.. Filings and briefs (trap): No courtesy copies. File each exhibit as a separate ECF attachment (e.g., ECF No. 4-1, 4-2) with a brief description; exhibits lumped into one attachment may have to be refiled. Submit complete deposition transcripts, not excerpts. Follow Local Rule word and page limits, and do not file a separate motion for each count to gain briefing. Extension requests, by motion or letter, must come well before the deadline. Cite unpublished opinions with the case number and any available Westlaw or Lexis cite; omitting either to save space is not allowed. Hyperlinked, searchable briefs and exhibits are preferred.

docs.t: Judge Nancy E. Brasel (D. Minn.) — Oral argument
docs.x: Judge Nancy E. Brasel, D. Minn.. Oral argument: Arrive at least 15 minutes early. Stand at the podium and address the court and counsel with civility and formality. Each side typically gets 30 minutes, including on summary judgment, preliminary injunction, and Daubert motions; with multiple motions the court sets the time. Contact the deputy if you need more. Focus on key issues rather than repeating the facts in the briefs. Bring copies of any PowerPoint for opposing counsel and two for the court. New case law must go to opposing counsel first, with two copies for the court if submitted the day of argument.

docs.t: Judge Nancy E. Brasel (D. Minn.) — Motions in limine (trap)
docs.x: Judge Nancy E. Brasel, D. Minn.. Motions in limine (trap): No more than five motions in limine without extraordinary circumstances and prior permission, each on one discrete issue. Supporting and opposing briefs are capped at 3,000 words, and no replies are allowed. The judge typically rules on motions in limine after the pretrial conference.

docs.t: Judge Nancy E. Brasel (D. Minn.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge Nancy E. Brasel, D. Minn.. Trial: A trial notice with detailed instructions issues at least four weeks before trial. The parties must meet and confer and jointly submit the agreed jury instructions, and stipulate to as many exhibits as possible. The judge conducts voir dire using standard questions and case-specific questions submitted by the parties; counsel may get to propose more. Trial days run 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. with two 15-minute breaks and an hour for lunch; have enough witnesses to fill each day until 5:00 p.m. Stand and use the counsel-table microphones for objections. Video recordings must be pre-edited, with disputes raised by motion in limine. Contacting jurors after trial requires Judge Brasel’s written permission in all cases.

docs.t: Judge Nancy E. Brasel (D. Minn.) — Settlement conferences
docs.x: Judge Nancy E. Brasel, D. Minn.. Settlement conferences: All settlement conferences go to the magistrate judge, and more than one may be held.

docs.t: Judge Patrick J. Schiltz (D. Minn.) — Dispositive motion scheduling (trap)
docs.x: Judge Patrick J. Schiltz, D. Minn.. Dispositive motion scheduling (trap): The dispositive motion deadline is always a “heard by” date. Contact the courtroom deputy three to four months before the deadline to get a hearing date in time. For a motion in lieu of an answer (such as a Rule 12(b)(6) motion), call as soon as possible after service, not on the day the answer is due. Arguments may be set any day of the week; there is no motions day. Nondispositive motions go to the magistrate judge, scheduled through that judge’s courtroom deputy. Before calling to schedule summary judgment, confer about cross-motions. The judge issues a briefing order for cross-motions that modifies the Local Rule deadlines, and all summary judgment motions are argued at one hearing.

docs.t: Judge Patrick J. Schiltz (D. Minn.) — Default, Markman, and Daubert (trap)
docs.x: Judge Patrick J. Schiltz, D. Minn.. Default, Markman, and Daubert (trap): The judge personally hears Rule 55(b)(2) default judgment motions, which are dispositive; first ask the Clerk to enter default under Rule 55(a). Markman motions are heard by the judge after a required informal pre-Markman conference. A Daubert motion that would knock out a claim or defense must be brought with the dispositive motion and argued in the same memoranda, and the two count as one motion for the Local Rule 7.1(f) word limit. A Daubert motion that only limits trial testimony is brought as a motion in limine under the trial notice, which issues after dispositive motions are resolved.

docs.t: Judge Patrick J. Schiltz (D. Minn.) — Briefing (trap)
docs.x: Judge Patrick J. Schiltz, D. Minn.. Briefing (trap): Motions to enlarge word limits are highly disfavored; file them in advance under Local Rule 7.1(f)(1)(D) and don’t file the brief until the request is granted. Before moving or stipulating to change a briefing schedule, contact the courtroom deputy for instructions. Multiple summary judgment motions filed at about the same time count as one for word limits (Local Rule 7.1(c)(4)). No motions to strike except under Rule 12(f) directed at a pleading; motions to strike affidavits, memoranda, or other supporting materials are not authorized. Under Local Rule 7.1(k), don’t file or serve unpublished opinions unless unavailable on CM/ECF, Westlaw, or LEXIS.

docs.t: Judge Patrick J. Schiltz (D. Minn.) — Courtesy copies (trap)
docs.x: Judge Patrick J. Schiltz, D. Minn.. Courtesy copies (trap): Deliver one courtesy copy of memoranda and supporting documents, three-hole punched and unstapled, with supporting documents tabbed in a three-ring binder. Courtesy copies of sealed or redacted filings must be unredacted. Note the docket number on each copy (the CM/ECF header works).

docs.t: Judge Patrick J. Schiltz (D. Minn.) — Oral argument (trap)
docs.x: Judge Patrick J. Schiltz, D. Minn.. Oral argument (trap): No time limits; argument continues until the judge’s questions are answered and counsel’s points are made. The judge reads the briefs and uses argument for back-and-forth, so be ready for detailed questions, including about the record. PowerPoint may not be used to summarize or restate arguments or add new arguments or evidence, only to highlight particular parts of the record. Arrive 15 minutes early; hearings start at or slightly before the scheduled time. Splitting argument between two attorneys, especially to give a newer lawyer experience, is fine. Give new authority offered at argument to the court and opposing counsel. docs.t: Judge Patrick J. Schiltz (D. Minn.) — Motions in limine and jury instructions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Patrick J. Schiltz, D. Minn.. Motions in limine and jury instructions (trap): No more than five motions in limine per party without prior permission, each limited to one discrete issue; supporting and opposing briefs capped at 3000 words; no replies. Don’t use them to reargue dispositive motions. Rulings are typically from the bench at the pretrial conference. Meet and confer and jointly file one set of proposed jury instructions, each citing current supporting authority. The judge prefers Eighth Circuit model instructions, using O’Malley to fill gaps or where it is better.

docs.t: Judge Patrick J. Schiltz (D. Minn.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge Patrick J. Schiltz, D. Minn.. Trial: A trial notice with detailed instructions issues about 90 days before a civil trial. Pretrial conferences are typically Fridays and trials start Mondays. The judge conducts voir dire. In criminal cases counsel usually get 10 minutes afterward; in civil cases counsel usually get no voir dire and instead propose additional questions at sidebar. Trial days generally run 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., with two 15-minute breaks and lunch from 12:00 to 1:30 p.m. Have witnesses to fill each day, and give 24 hours’ notice of each day’s witnesses. Mark exhibits per the trial notice and have paper copies to show witnesses before admission; admitted exhibits may be published electronically. docs.t: Judge Patrick J. Schiltz (D. Minn.) — Settlement and chambers contact
docs.x: Judge Patrick J. Schiltz, D. Minn.. Settlement and chambers contact: All settlement conferences go to the magistrate judge, requested through that judge’s courtroom deputy; a private mediator may be used instead. The courtroom deputy answers questions about the judge’s policies and preferences but gives no legal advice.

docs.t: Judge Paul A. Magnuson (D. Minn.) — Motion scheduling (trap)
docs.x: Judge Paul A. Magnuson, D. Minn.. Motion scheduling (trap): Call the courtroom deputy (651-848-1150 or Magnuson_chambers@mnd.uscourts.gov; not the law clerk) for an argument date only when all motion papers are ready. The date is held for only two business days, so file promptly. Argument on dispositive motions is at least 42 days after filing, and usually later. If the motion is not fully briefed under the Local Rules schedule, the hearing may be canceled and reset. You meet the scheduling-order dispositive motion deadline if you file your motion papers and get a date from the deputy before it.

docs.t: Judge Paul A. Magnuson (D. Minn.) — Daubert motions
docs.x: Judge Paul A. Magnuson, D. Minn.. Daubert motions: Judge Magnuson, not the magistrate judge, typically hears Daubert motions. Call the deputy to schedule after expert reports are served but well before the motion in limine deadline.

docs.t: Judge Paul A. Magnuson (D. Minn.) — Hearings

Either side may sit at either table. Expect no more than 20 minutes per side on summary judgment, varying with the case. The judge reads the papers in advance, so do not repeat the facts. New case law at argument must be given to opposing counsel, with extra copies for the court.

docs.t: Judge Paul A. Magnuson (D. Minn.) — Trial (trap)
docs.x: Judge Paul A. Magnuson, D. Minn.. Trial (trap): The parties must meet and confer and jointly submit an agreed exhibit list. docs.t: Judge Paul A. Magnuson (D. Minn.) — Settlement conferences
docs.x: Judge Paul A. Magnuson, D. Minn.. Settlement conferences: Referred to the magistrate judge or a special master. Request one at any time through the deputy or by letter to the magistrate judge; more than one is allowed.

Tell the courtroom deputy about all pending motions in the case, and related cases with related motions, so they can be heard together.

docs.t: Judge Susan Richard Nelson (D. Minn.) — Special motions (trap)

docs.t: Judge Susan Richard Nelson (D. Minn.) — Written submissions and courtesy copies (trap)
docs.x: Judge Susan Richard Nelson, D. Minn.. Written submissions and courtesy copies (trap): Follow the Local Rules’ word count and format rules. Request extra pages or words by letter filed on ECF before filing the brief. Send two courtesy copies of motion papers, tabbed, three-hole punched, and unstapled (binders welcome for voluminous filings), to arrive no later than the day after e-filing. When a deadline falls on a weekend, file the following Monday. Use the judge’s full name, Susan Richard Nelson, in proposed orders.

docs.t: Judge Susan Richard Nelson (D. Minn.) — Settlement conferences
docs.x: Judge Susan Richard Nelson, D. Minn.. Settlement conferences: Most settlement conferences go to the magistrate judge; request one any time. More than one is allowed.

The court schedules a hearing only if it decides one is necessary after reviewing the briefs.

docs.x: Judge M. Hannah Lauck, E.D. Va.. Generative AI disclosure (trap): Any party that uses generative artificial intelligence to prepare a filing must identify that use in the filing and certify that it has reviewed all citations for accuracy.

docs.x: Judge Christopher L. Ray, S.D. Ga.. Motions court; no informal requests (trap): Magistrate Judge Ray will not consider informal requests to the courtroom deputy or chambers for rulings on any issue, including extensions of time. Any ruling of any kind requires a motion on the docket. Letter briefs are not accepted except under the informal discovery conference and settlement conference procedures. Inquiries go to courtroom deputy Molly Davenport (molly_davenport@gas.uscourts.gov, 912-650-4035).

docs.t: Judge Christopher L. Ray (S.D. Ga.) — Discovery disputes: conference first (trap)
docs.x: Judge Christopher L. Ray, S.D. Ga.. Discovery disputes: conference first (trap): No discovery motion may be filed without the court’s permission after an informal discovery dispute video conference. This covers Rule 37 motions, Rule 26 protective-order motions, and Rule 45 motions to quash or compel when compliance is in this District, but not Rule 26(a)(1)(B)-exempt proceedings, cases with an unrepresented party, or Daubert motions and motions to strike experts (though the court may apply it to any dispute on notice). File the Motion for an Informal Discovery Dispute Conference on ECF (Civil – Motions – Motion for Informal Discovery Dispute Conference) using the court’s form, giving at least three mutually agreeable dates and times within two weeks of filing. Before asking, counsel must meet and confer under LR 26.5, which the court expects to mean actually speaking with each other (in

docs.t: Judge Christopher L. Ray (S.D. Ga.) — Discovery letter briefs (trap)
docs.x: Judge Christopher L. Ray, S.D. Ga.. Discovery letter briefs (trap): At least 24 hours before the conference, each side emails the courtroom deputy a letter brief addressed to Judge Ray (not filed on the docket), served on all counsel: no more than three pages single-spaced plus up to ten pages of exhibits, factual and non-argumentative, naming who will appear. Only disputes in the letters are considered, and be ready to raise all pending discovery issues: failing to raise an existing dispute may be treated as a waiver.

docs.t: Judge Christopher L. Ray (S.D. Ga.) — After the discovery conference
docs.x: Judge Christopher L. Ray, S.D. Ga.. After the discovery conference: The conference is not on the record; the court may not issue a written ruling and may just note the conference in a text entry. If the dispute is not resolved, the parties have ten days to file a discovery motion.

docs.t: Judge Christopher L. Ray (S.D. Ga.) — Settlement conferences
docs.x: Judge Christopher L. Ray, S.D. Ga.. Settlement conferences: On consent, parties may move for a settlement conference with Judge Ray, offering at least four mutually agreeable dates no later than 2 months after filing. The case must be ready for meaningful settlement discussions. All parties, including at least one person with full settlement authority, must attend in person with counsel; remote attendance only for good cause (the worksheet says a substantial showing, and mere convenience is not enough). At least one week before, jointly email the Settlement Conference Worksheet to the courtroom deputy (do not file it). Written settlement statements are not required unless the court gives at least 48 hours’ notice, and then follow the letter-brief length limits.

docs.t: Judge Christopher L. Ray (S.D. Ga.) — Search warrant applications
docs.x: Judge Christopher L. Ray, S.D. Ga.. Search warrant applications: Search warrant applications are heard each business day at 2:00 p.m.; agents and the U.S. Attorney’s Office must submit all papers by 4:30 p.m. the preceding business day, absent truly extraordinary circumstances. Email each application to the courtroom deputy as one text-searchable PDF with the application, supporting documents, and affidavits in the order the AUSA expects to discuss them. Changes after the 4:30 p.m. deadline may delay processing; emergency requests need a showing of need by email or phone first.

docs.t: Judge Scott W. Skavdahl (D. Wyo.) — Case management plan
docs.x: Judge Scott W. Skavdahl, D. Wyo.. Case management plan: The Joint Case Management Plan form asks for, among other things, the Rule 26(f) attendees, parties and parent entities (for recusal), related cases, a nature-of-the-case statement of 2 pages or less, and a jurisdiction statement; in diversity cases, state every party’s citizenship, including each partner or member of a partnership or LLC. Propose expert disclosure, fact discovery, and trial dates on the expectation that trial occurs within approximately nine months of the Initial Pretrial Conference, absent unusual circumstances. The plan is subject to revision at the conference.

docs.t: Judge Scott W. Skavdahl (D. Wyo.) — Exhibits and the final pretrial order (trap)
docs.x: Judge Scott W. Skavdahl, D. Wyo.. Exhibits and the final pretrial order (trap): Exhibit lists in the final pretrial order sort objections into Category A (admissible without further proof), B (objections other than foundation, such as hearsay or relevance), and C (foundation, identification, or authenticity only). Failing to mark a foundation objection waives it, and a party that proves foundation over objection may move for fees and costs. Before trial, give the court one hard copy (tabbed ringed binder with the exhibit list in front) and one electronic copy of all exhibits. Provide electronic trial exhibits for JERS on a USB drive, DVD, or CD to the Clerk’s Office at least 7 days before trial (PDF/JPG/BMP/TIF/GIF; AVI/WMV/MPG/MP3/MP4/WMA/WAV; files no larger than 500MB). Five business days before trial, email the court reporter (megan_strawn@wyd.uscourts.gov) exhibit and witness lists

docs.t: Judge Scott W. Skavdahl (D. Wyo.) — Depositions at trial (trap)
docs.x: Judge Scott W. Skavdahl, D. Wyo.. Depositions at trial (trap): Notify opposing counsel of deposition offers at least 10 business days before trial; objections or counter-designations are due at least 5 business days before trial, and unresolved differences go to the court in writing at least 3 business days before trial.

docs.t: Judge Scott W. Skavdahl (D. Wyo.) — Witnesses
docs.x: Judge Scott W. Skavdahl, D. Wyo.. Witnesses: Listing a “will call” witness guarantees the witness’s presence at trial. In jury cases, give the court an estimate of each witness’s time on the stand at least 7 days before trial, and tell opposing counsel during trial which witnesses you will call the next day.

docs.t: Judge Scott W. Skavdahl (D. Wyo.) — Jury instructions and voir dire (trap)
docs.x: Judge Scott W. Skavdahl, D. Wyo.. Jury instructions and voir dire (trap): Proposed voir dire, jury instructions, and verdict forms are due 7 days before trial. The court provides stock instructions; submit substantive instructions (and any requested changes to stock ones) in three sets with citations: Set A agreed, Set B plaintiff’s disputed, Set C defendant’s disputed. File them and also email them to chambers (wyojudgesws@wyd.uscourts.gov) in Word or WordPerfect. At the same time, file a brief, noncontentious joint statement of the case (“Plaintiff contends . . . ; Defendant contends . . .” where the parties can’t agree).

docs.t: Judge Scott W. Skavdahl (D. Wyo.) — Jury selection
docs.x: Judge Scott W. Skavdahl, D. Wyo.. Jury selection: Fourteen jurors are seated for voir dire; after the panel is passed for cause, each side exercises up to three peremptory challenges in writing, alternating starting with plaintiff, and the first eight unchallenged jurors are the jury. Each side gets thirty minutes of its own voir dire after the court’s. Jury trials start at 9:00 a.m. in Casper.

docs.t: Judge Scott W. Skavdahl (D. Wyo.) — Bench trials: findings and conclusions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Scott W. Skavdahl, D. Wyo.. Bench trials: findings and conclusions (trap): Plaintiff submits proposed findings of fact and conclusions of law at least ten days before trial and defendant five days before trial; file them and email them to chambers in Word or WordPerfect. Plaintiff’s facts go in simple declarative sentences in numbered paragraphs, with no recitation of testimony or admissions, no pejoratives or legal conclusions, so each sentence can be admitted or denied; legal contentions go in numbered paragraphs, each followed by authority. Defendant’s response admits or denies each sentence using plaintiff’s numbering, then adds its own affirmative facts and responsive legal contentions in the same format.

docs.t: Judge Scott W. Skavdahl (D. Wyo.) — Bench trials: written direct testimony (trap)
docs.x: Judge Scott W. Skavdahl, D. Wyo.. Bench trials: written direct testimony (trap): Expert witnesses and witnesses on significant technical matters give direct testimony by an unsworn narrative written statement (not Q&A), which the witness adopts under oath at trial and the party offers as an exhibit; live supplementation is limited and expected to be minimal. Not for adverse parties or subpoenaed witnesses. Exhibits are not attached to the statements but pre-marked and exchanged as usual. The expert procedure requires exchange and filing no later than 14 days before trial (or as the initial pretrial order sets); the bench-trial pretrial form says 7 days before the final pretrial conference.

docs.t: Judge Josh Divine (E.D. Mo.) — Contacts and emergencies
docs.x: Judge Josh Divine, E.D. Mo.. Contacts and emergencies: Routine matters go to the case management team; case-specific matters go by email to the law clerk assigned by the case number’s last digit (1–3 Ethan Wang, 4–6 William Bock IV, 7–9 Vance Kelley; for 0, use the last nonzero digit). For an emergency motion needing a hearing on the record, call chambers and follow up by email to Divine_Chambers@moed.uscourts.gov. For same-day relief, call the assigned clerk.

docs.t: Judge Josh Divine (E.D. Mo.) — Briefs: limits and format (trap)
docs.x: Judge Josh Divine, E.D. Mo.. Briefs: limits and format (trap): Memoranda supporting or opposing a motion are limited to 15 pages and replies to 8 pages, with one-inch margins, double spacing (except footnotes), and 11-point Century Schoolbook throughout. Anything over 10 pages needs a table of contents and table of authorities, with asterisks in the left margin marking the chief authorities. Start the heading of any motion needing consent (such as an extension) with “Opposed,” “Unopposed,” or a variation, and end it with a certificate of conference giving the date, time, manner, and participants (not needed for dispositive or injunction motions). Motions lacking a required certificate may be stricken. Failing to oppose a motion or respond to an argument may be treated as a concession. Proposed orders are filed as a PDF attachment and emailed to the assigned clerk in word-processing forma

docs.t: Judge Josh Divine (E.D. Mo.) — Pleadings: one-document rule (trap)
docs.x: Judge Josh Divine, E.D. Mo.. Pleadings: one-document rule (trap): After filing a complaint, counterclaim, or crossclaim, send opposing counsel a .doc or .docx copy. Answers must be prepared in that Word document, with each response in a non-numbered paragraph directly below the allegation (not for pro se parties or appeals). Amended pleadings must include a redline against the original as the final attachment. A party opposing a motion to dismiss must say whether amendment can cure the problem; otherwise the court is disinclined to allow a later amendment.

docs.t: Judge Josh Divine (E.D. Mo.) — Extensions and case management order (trap)
docs.x: Judge Josh Divine, E.D. Mo.. Extensions and case management order (trap): Extensions are strongly discouraged; a first extension over three weeks, or any later extension, requires exceptional or compelling circumstances. Joint stipulations to extend or reschedule are not honored; file a motion at least four business days before the first affected date stating the current date, time requested, grounds, prior extensions, effect on other deadlines, and a proposed schedule after conferring. Case management order changes outside Rule 29 need a motion with an updated draft order at least four business days before the deadline and exceptional circumstances, which do not include press of business, slow discovery, or delay in starting discovery. Expect trial in the order’s window.

docs.t: Judge Josh Divine (E.D. Mo.) — Multiple parties and summary judgment (trap)
docs.x: Judge Josh Divine, E.D. Mo.. Multiple parties and summary judgment (trap): Co-parties must file joint motions and joint memoranda on the same or similar issues, under the same page limits. Each movant may file only one summary judgment motion and one Rule 702/703 motion covering all experts. Multiple movants file one consolidated statement of material facts and respondents one consolidated response. Send the statement to opponents in .doc/.docx; the response is written in that document, with each disputed fact explained in a non-numbered paragraph below it. Unanswered facts are deemed admitted; additional facts go in a separate, numbered filing. A joint statement of uncontested facts is due within 10 days after summary judgment briefing is complete. The court prefers dispositive motions fully briefed 120 days before trial.

docs.t: Judge Josh Divine (E.D. Mo.) — Discovery disputes (trap)
docs.x: Judge Josh Divine, E.D. Mo.. Discovery disputes (trap): No discovery motion without the court’s approval. After meeting and conferring (letters, emails, or texts don’t count), email the assigned clerk to request a telephone conference, with a certificate of conference. The same applies to disputes with nonparties, who must be told of these procedures; incarcerated pro se cases may confer in writing and file without approval. After the conference is scheduled, the movant files a one- to two-page single-spaced motion and the opponent a one- to two-page response within three business days, raising no new issues; include the disputed request and objection. Motions to compel are due no more than 11 days after the discovery deadline. docs.t: Judge Josh Divine (E.D. Mo.) — Sealing, protective orders, and filing
docs.x: Judge Josh Divine, E.D. Mo.. Sealing, protective orders, and filing: Email proposed protective orders to the assigned clerk; any that mention sealing must require the parties to ask the court to remove sealed documents within thirty days after the case ends, or they will be unsealed. The court strongly prefers redaction to sealing. Filings must be text-searchable PDFs converted directly from word processing; OCR any scanned exhibits. Edit exhibits to the pertinent parts and highlight them. No courtesy copies except a courtesy copy of exhibits brought to trial.

docs.t: Judge Josh Divine (E.D. Mo.) — Generative AI certificate (trap)
docs.x: Judge Josh Divine, E.D. Mo.. Generative AI certificate (trap): Every attorney and pro se litigant must file, with the notice of appearance, an “AI notice” (CM/ECF Notices) certifying that no filing will be drafted by generative AI or that any AI-drafted language will be fully checked by a human using print reporters or traditional legal databases. Sanctions for fake or misrepresented cases can include fines, striking, and dismissal.

docs.t: Judge Josh Divine (E.D. Mo.) — Rule 16, ADR, and settlement
docs.x: Judge Josh Divine, E.D. Mo.. Rule 16, ADR, and settlement: The court sets a Rule 16 conference after all defendants answer. The parties submit one joint plan, signed by all, on the judge’s Case Management Order template, with disputes in an appendix; plaintiff initiates. Track ranges: expedited (disposition within 12 months, 120 days of discovery), standard (18 months, 180–240 days), complex (24 months, 240–360 days). Lead trial counsel must attend. Civil cases (except habeas, Social Security, and bankruptcy appeals) are referred to ADR; plaintiff’s counsel is lead counsel unless the parties agree otherwise. A neutral not on the certified list needs a motion and special expertise. ADR extensions need a motion at least four business days before the deadline. On settlement, notify the court immediately; dismissal papers are due within 30 days.

docs.t: Judge Josh Divine (E.D. Mo.) — Pretrial filings (trap)
docs.x: Judge Josh Divine, E.D. Mo.. Pretrial filings (trap): Civil trials sit on a three-week docket; be ready on day one and on twenty-four hours’ notice. By 10 days before trial: joint stipulation of uncontested facts, one-page joint case summary, motions in limine (all in one document per party; responses in 7 days), exhibit and witness lists, exhibits delivered to the clerk, deposition and discovery designations, and objections to demonstratives (which are listed 14 days and exchanged 10 days before trial). Plaintiff numbers exhibits from 1 and defendants from 1000; the list must flag business records to be authenticated under FRE 902(11) or (12). Exhibit and designation objections are due 7 days before trial or may be waived. Voir dire questions, 404(b) notices, and unresolved recording-transcript disputes are due 7 days before trial. docs.t: Judge Josh Divine (E.D. Mo.) — Trial conduct (trap)
docs.x: Judge Josh Divine, E.D. Mo.. Trial conduct (trap): The court conducts voir dire; counsel may get up to 20 minutes after. Openings and closings are limited to 20 minutes per side. Raise preliminary matters 15 minutes before the trial day, at lunch, or at day’s end, never when the jury is ready. Objections are a word or phrase with no argument before the jury; ask for a further record at the next recess. No re-cross unless new matter arises on redirect, do not call a witness an “expert,” and don’t talk with your witness between tender for cross and redirect. Send next-day witness lists by 7:00 p.m. Stand when speaking. Only attorneys may use devices without approval (silenced); non-attorneys power off. Schedule ELMO training before trial (not on trial day) and bring your own audio player.

docs.t: Judge Daniel Calabretta (E.D. Cal.) — Hearings and appearances (trap)
docs.x: Judge Daniel Calabretta, E.D. Cal.. Hearings and appearances (trap): Civil law and motion on designated Thursdays at 1:30 p.m.; criminal law and motion on Thursdays at 9:00 a.m.; Courtroom 7, 14th floor, Sacramento. Dates are not reserved, but get available dates by emailing the courtroom deputy, Gabriel Michel (gmichel@caed.uscourts.gov). Bail-review motions are not noticed on the criminal calendar. Oral argument on all motions is in person. In civil cases, joint requests to appear remotely must be made at least one week before the hearing and are generally disfavored. Civil papers must say whether the party wants the motion decided without oral argument; the court may take any motion under submission under Local Rule 230(g) and will say so by minute order before the hearing. docs.t: Judge Daniel Calabretta (E.D. Cal.) — Briefing and page limits (trap)
docs.x: Judge Daniel Calabretta, E.D. Cal.. Briefing and page limits (trap): Civil and criminal: 12-point font, footnotes no more than two sizes smaller, and a sans serif font such as Arial or Helvetica encouraged. Moving and opposition briefs are capped at 25 pages and replies at 15 without prior leave, granted only for good cause; pages over the limit will not be considered. No supplemental briefs or sur-replies without prior leave. Paginate multi-page exhibits internally starting at 1 and cite them by exhibit and page (e.g., Ex. A at 7).

docs.t: Judge Daniel Calabretta (E.D. Cal.) — Civil meet and confer (trap)
docs.x: Judge Daniel Calabretta, E.D. Cal.. Civil meet and confer (trap): In represented civil cases, counsel must meet and confer before filing any motion to discuss its substance and possible resolution, settling minor procedural matters along the way. The notice of motion must certify that meet-and-confer efforts were exhausted, with a very brief summary; noncompliant motions are summarily denied without prejudice.

docs.t: Judge Daniel Calabretta (E.D. Cal.) — Summary judgment and cross-motions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Daniel Calabretta, E.D. Cal.. Summary judgment and cross-motions (trap): Read Local Rule 260. Before filing, meet and confer on stipulated facts and file them as a Joint Statement of Undisputed Facts, plus a Separate Statement for facts not stipulated. The nonmovant reproduces and responds and may file a concise Statement of Disputed Facts; the movant responds to that but may not reply to the nonmovant’s response. At least 28 days before the dispositive-motion deadline, meet and confer about cross-motions. If cross-motions are planned, only four briefs are allowed: plaintiff’s opening (25 pages) at least 14 days before the deadline, noticed for hearing at least 42 days out; defendant’s opposition and cross-motion (35 pages) 14 days later; plaintiff’s reply and opposition (20 pages) 14 days later; and defendant’s reply (10 pages) 10 days later. docs.t: Judge Daniel Calabretta (E.D. Cal.) — Proposed orders and ex parte applications
docs.x: Judge Daniel Calabretta, E.D. Cal.. Proposed orders and ex parte applications: Proposed orders are not required with civil motions except for TROs and preliminary injunctions; also submit proposed consent decrees where applicable and proposed findings and conclusions after a bench trial. Any required proposed order must follow Local Rule 137(b) and be emailed in Word to DJCorders@caed.uscourts.gov. Ex parte applications are usually decided on the papers. Before filing, contact the courtroom deputy and the opposing party; the papers must say whether an opposition will be filed and include an affidavit explaining the need for the order, why a stipulation could not be obtained, and why the matter cannot be noticed under Local Rule 230.

docs.t: Judge Daniel Calabretta (E.D. Cal.) — Sealing and protective orders (trap)
docs.x: Judge Daniel Calabretta, E.D. Cal.. Sealing and protective orders (trap): Nothing is sealed or filed redacted without prior court approval (except Local Rule 140 redactions). Sealing or redaction requests about the record on a motion Judge Calabretta will decide go to Judge Calabretta, not the magistrate judge. The request must say whether it is opposed; if it is opposed or silent, other parties must file an opposition or non-opposition within three days of service. File the Notice of Request electronically, and email the request, a proposed order in Word, and the documents to DJCorders@caed.uscourts.gov; once the order is entered, email the documents to ApprovedSealed@caed.uscourts.gov. Discovery protective orders do not govern sealing on the public docket, and only the proponent of sealing may request it. Give the designating party enough advance notice to seek sealing before you file

docs.t: Judge Daniel Calabretta (E.D. Cal.) — Extensions and continuances
docs.x: Judge Daniel Calabretta, E.D. Cal.. Extensions and continuances: Stipulations extending deadlines or modifying rules have no effect until approved. File well in advance, listing the existing date and all other set dates (discovery cutoff, last motion hearing date, pretrial conference, and trial), specific good-cause reasons, and any prior requests and their outcome. In civil cases, saying an extension “will promote settlement” is not enough; describe the status of negotiations with specificity. Stipulations continuing dispositive-motion dates (civil) or the trial date are disfavored.
